clue.text: Grating I had found in the river after Sunday

indicators.note: the river piece comes after the Sunday letter in the answer
the contraction for 'I had' is found sitting inside the river's name

parts.note: the Trent is a major river of the English Midlands
I'd, the contraction of 'I had', gives ID

explanation.surface: Someone notices a metal grille lying in a river, the day after Sunday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grating' looks like a noun for a grille but is the adjective; 'found in' signals the insertion and 'after' places the Sunday letter first.
explanation.definitionFit: A strident voice is harsh and rasping, just as a grating noise is.

clue.text: One not in favour of the gold article

parts.note: an article is a thing or item, an object
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Someone opposes the golden item on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is gold in heraldry; the pieces go in the reverse of the clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: An objector is a person who opposes or protests against something.

clue.text: Appeared in play as a brightly-coloured celestial body?

parts.note: a star is a body in the heavens
red is a vivid colour

explanation.surface: An actor appeared on stage dressed as a vivid star.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a red star; the two pieces swap round from clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who starred took a leading role in a stage production.

clue.text: Hikers disturbed a predatory bird

indicators.note: letters that are disturbed are thrown out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Walkers on a trail startled a bird of prey.
explanation.definitionFit: The shrike, or butcher-bird, impales its prey on thorns, a true hunter.

clue.text: Joint-t ornament

parts.note: the ankle is the joint between foot and leg
the letter t, given as it is

explanation.surface: A piece of jewellery shaped like a joint with a T attached.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as an odd word, 'Joint-t': the joint gives ANKLE and the extra t is added on.
explanation.definitionFit: An anklet is a decorative band or chain worn round the lower leg.

clue.text: How to be doubly sure of taking one's opportunity

definitions.text: How to be doubly sure of taking one's opportunity

parts.words: How to be doubly sure of taking one's opportunity
parts.note: seizing a chance is pictured literally as grabbing it with both arms' ends at once, which makes the grab doubly secure

explanation.definitionFit: To seize a chance eagerly is to grab it with full enthusiasm and no hesitation.

clue.text: Too many to count-or none at all?

definitions.meaning: read literally, lacking any figure, having no count

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means innumerable, but read literally it means lacking a single figure.

clue.text: But he could play the part of a crook!

definitions.text: But he could play the part of a crook!

parts.words: But he could play the part of a crook!
parts.note: a performer of conventional, non-comic roles is called by a word meaning honest or not bent, yet he may well be cast as a villain

explanation.definitionFit: A serious dramatic performer, as opposed to a comedian, may still be cast as a villain.

clue.text: Way abounding in conflict

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
rife means widespread or abounding

explanation.surface: A road where trouble is everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Strife is bitter disagreement or fighting, a synonym for conflict.

clue.text: Lie Larry concocted, a form of playful satire

indicators.note: something concocted is made up, so the letters are mixed into a new form

explanation.surface: Larry made up a fib as a bit of gentle mockery.
explanation.definitionFit: Raillery is good-humoured teasing or banter, mockery without malice.

clue.text: Blimey, it's a French horn!

definitions.meaning: the French word for a horn

explanation.definitionFit: It is a Cockney exclamation of surprise, and also the French word for the brass instrument.

clue.text: Instant importance?

definitions.meaning: a very brief point in time
significance, as in a matter of great weight

explanation.definitionFit: It is a brief point of time, and also significance, as in 'of great moment'.

clue.text: Very exciting storm?

definitions.meaning: as in a thunderstorm with lightning, described by the word

explanation.definitionFit: It means thrilling, and also describes a storm full of lightning.

clue.text: Stick a potter uses

parts.note: the potter is not a maker of pots but a snooker player who pots balls with a long rod

explanation.definitionFit: A snooker player pots balls by striking them with a long tapered rod.

clue.text: Height of inferior articles certain to go round

indicators.note: the word for certain goes round the piece for inferior articles, enclosing it

parts.note: sure means certain
tat is cheap, shoddy goods

explanation.surface: How tall a pile of junk stands when sure to be encircled.
explanation.walkthrough: Tat is British slang for cheap, tasteless goods; 'to go round' signals the enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Stature is a person's natural height when standing.

clue.text: River flowing through pastureland

indicators.note: the river's name runs through the letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A stream winds through grazing fields.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a river in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ure is a Yorkshire waterway that feeds the Ouse.

clue.text: Make an impressive design in blue maybe but it is only superficial

indicators.note: the design word is placed inside the word for blue

parts.note: the sky is blue, as an example
to etch is to cut or impress a design into a surface

explanation.surface: An artist engraves a striking design in blue, but it only scratches the surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the insertion; 'but it is only' is linking, so the definition is the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketchy account is rough and lacking detail, treating things only at surface level.

clue.text: Kay, with inordinate greed and ease, say, had a dish of rice

parts.note: the letter K is spelt kay

indicators.note: inordinate means disordered here, so the letters are jumbled
say signals that the word is to be heard, giving its sound

parts.note: spoken aloud it sounds like the letters E E

explanation.surface: Kay, greedy and relaxed, ate a plate of rice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inordinate' turns GREED into EDGER; 'say' makes EASE sound like 'E's', giving EE.
explanation.definitionFit: Kedgeree is an Anglo-Indian dish of rice, smoked fish and egg.

clue.text: See tide's turning by the river!

indicators.note: the letters turn about into a new order

explanation.surface: Watch the tide change on the riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: Teesside is the area of north-east England around the river Tees.
explanation.definitionFit: The region takes its name from lying along the banks of the Tees in north-east England.

clue.text: Forget abominably lean run

indicators.note: done abominably, the letters end up horribly out of order

explanation.surface: A runner forgets a dreadful thin jog.
explanation.definitionFit: To unlearn is to deliberately put a habit or knowledge out of one's mind.

clue.text: News of how murder victim died?

definitions.meaning: the victim was shot, with a round lodged inside

explanation.definitionFit: It is a short news report, and split up says a round was lodged in the body.

clue.text: Roomy suit?

parts.note: not a spacious outfit but a suit named after a sitting room, everyday daywear for men

explanation.definitionFit: A man's ordinary business suit shares its name with a sitting room.

clue.text: Plant provided meals, as reported, the French conclude

indicators.note: the French article comes at the end
as reported signals the word for meals is heard, not seen

parts.note: teas are light afternoon or evening meals
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: A plant supplied meals, it's said, and the French finish things off.
explanation.walkthrough: TEAS sounds like TEAZ; LE, French for 'the', concludes. Teazle is a variant spelling of teasel, a prickly plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The teasel is a tall, thistle-like flowering plant once used to raise the nap on cloth.

clue.text: Radio presenter's bird found the river first

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
a jay is a bird of the crow family

explanation.surface: A broadcaster's pet bird discovered the river before anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay; 'first' puts the river ahead of the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A deejay, a DJ, plays records on air.

clue.text: Support either the home or the away match

definitions.meaning: a limb that holds something up

definitions.text: either the home or the away match
definitions.meaning: one of the two games in a two-part tie

explanation.definitionFit: It is a supporting limb, and also one half of a two-match football tie.

clue.text: Hard to remove red u-boat

indicators.note: to remove is to shift the letters to new positions

explanation.surface: A red submarine proving difficult to dislodge.
explanation.definitionFit: Obdurate means stubbornly unyielding, hard of heart.

clue.text: In winter sat Zoe, the substitute

indicators.note: the answer sits within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Zoe sat in during the winter, standing in for someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz means an imitation used in place of the real thing.

clue.text: One taking each issue as it comes

definitions.text: One taking each issue as it comes

parts.words: One taking each issue as it comes
parts.note: sounds like someone relaxed about problems, but describes a person who gets every edition of a periodical

explanation.definitionFit: A habitual subscriber or buyer reads every edition of a publication.
